title: Derived internal Hom commutes with restriction to opens
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], let $K,L$ be objects of the derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $U\subseteq X$ be open, with restrictions $K|_U,L|_U\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ computed termwise on representing complexes. Then there is a canonical isomorphism $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(K|_U,L|_U)\cong R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)|_U$ in $D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

proof.text: Choose complex representatives Kc and Lc using essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q. The source-library SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian supplies the instance already used by derivedInternalHom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Apply the existing functorial K-injective construction [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] to Lc, obtaining Ic and the quasi-isomorphism eta. Invert Q(eta) and compose with the representative isomorphism of L to get Q(Ic) ≅ L. Apply derivedInternalHom_obj_iso [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to identify derived Hom on X with Q(homComplex Kc Ic).

Let F be open restriction and Fc its termwise complex functor. By kInjective_of_restrict_open [lem-sc-derived-k-injective-restrict-open], Fc(Ic) is K-injective. The exact-functor comparison F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors identifies Q(Fc(Kc)) and Q(Fc(Ic)) with the derived restrictions of K and L. Apply derivedInternalHom_obj_iso [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the localized site to compute the local derived Hom by Q(homComplex(Fc(Kc),Fc(Ic))).

Apply the ordinary complex isomorphism homComplex_restrict_open [lem-sc-hom-complex-restrict-open] to Kc and Ic. Map it with the localization functor Q on the localized site. Compose with the inverse of F.mapDerivedCategoryFactors on homComplex Kc Ic, and then with the inverse of F.mapDerivedCategory.mapIso applied to the global derived-Hom computation from Step 1. Prepend the local computation from Step 2. This explicit composition has precisely the source and target of the theorem.
